functions.name: VdfLoad_Update
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::Update - MAP LOADING STATE MACHINE (VdfLoad.cpp:347)
Driven once per frame with deltaMs. Dispatches on this->m_state (VdfLoadState).

Flow:
  0  INIT
  1  LOAD_CONTENT      inline here - waits on map content pack, pushes m_mapDef to portal ctx
  2  LOAD_MANIFEST     inline here - waits MapPortalContext::IsReady(), arms 300s server wait
  3  SERVER_WAIT       inline here - waits m_serverReady (set by VdfLoad__OnMapServerReady)
  4  SERVER_WAIT_ERROR terminal (timeout)
  5  MAP_DOWNLOAD      -> VdfLoad__State05_MapDownload
  6  DOWNLOAD_ERROR    terminal
  7  MAP_STREAM        -> VdfLoad__State07_MapStream
  8  MAP_STREAM_ERROR  terminal
  9  MODELS_STREAM     -> VdfLoad__State09_ModelsStream
  10 MAP_ASSET_STREAM  inline here - min() of per-map completion until 1.0, then preloads char assets
  11 AGENT_STREAM      -> VdfLoad__State11_AgentStream
  12 READY_WAIT        -> VdfLoad__State12_ReadyWait
  13 READY             terminal - map is playable

Hang detection: each state arms the NEXT state's budget, which that state ticks
down by deltaMs. On expiry it logs "Map load hang on <STATE> detected" and force-
completes rather than stalling. Budgets set in VdfLoad__Reset (retail): models 60s,
asset 15s, agent 120s, ready-wait 1s, download 10s.

functions.name: VdfLoad_State11_AgentStream
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad state 11: STATE_AGENT_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:926)
Arms m_readyWaitTimerMs = 1000 and ticks m_agentStreamTimerMs.
Waits for the agent-view to report ready, then for character loading to drain
(char count == 0) and VdfLoad__ArePreloadAssetsReady. Records metric 12
(total models) and 13 (char count). Pushes the terrain/env params into every
m_maps entry, then -> STATE_READY_WAIT.

functions.name: VdfLoad_State05_MapDownload
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad state 5: STATE_MAP_DOWNLOAD (VdfLoad.cpp:556)
Ticks m_mapDownloadTimerMs. Polls m_mapDownload; on failure -> state 6.
Rejects encrypted maps (mapDef flags & 0x20000000) when m_mapEncryptionKey is
NULL: "tried to enter an encrypted map without a key".
On success builds m_streamRequests (56-byte entries) and spawns one map-stream
object per request into m_maps, then -> STATE_MAP_STREAM.

functions.name: VdfLoad_State07_MapStream
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad state 7: STATE_MAP_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:691)
Arms m_modelsStreamBudgetMs -> m_modelsStreamTimerMs for the next state.
Polls each m_streamRequests[i] status (vtbl+48): 1/2/3 stamp metrics 5/6/7 and
re-issue with priority 100; 4 = done -> publishes the built map into m_maps[i];
5 = error -> state 8. Releases each request once consumed.
When all are done: VdfLoad__ActivateMapsAndBuildWorld, then STATE_MODELS_STREAM.

functions.name: VdfLoad_State09_ModelsStream
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad state 9: STATE_MODELS_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:766)
Arms m_assetStreamBudgetMs and ticks m_modelsStreamTimerMs.
For the first 6000ms (0x1770) it keeps re-sampling the global model counters to
establish m_modelLoadTotal; after that the total is frozen so the progress bar
cannot go backwards. m_modelCompletion is monotonic (never decreases).
Teleports (m_portalIndex != -1) take completion straight from the portal ctx.
Exits when completion >= 1.0 OR the timer expires (logs a hang), -> ASSET_STREAM.

functions.name: VdfLoad_State12_ReadyWait
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad state 12: STATE_READY_WAIT (VdfLoad.cpp:1003)
One-second settle: while m_readyWaitTimerMs > 0 it keeps pushing lighting/env
parameters into each map so the first presented frame is fully lit.
When it expires: closes the portal context, notifies the world view, marks each
map active (vtbl+168, arg 2) and -> STATE_READY. Map is now playable.

functions.name: VdfLoad_ActivateMapsAndBuildWorld
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::ActivateMapsAndBuildWorld (VdfLoad.cpp:1095)
Called once at the end of STATE_MAP_STREAM. Binds each streamed map to the
local player's agent, registers the map id with the audio/env systems, creates
the world renderer and seeds the camera from m_spawnPos.
Asserts !WorldView()->HasRenderer() on entry - the renderer must not exist yet.

functions.name: VdfLoad_BeginMap
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::BeginMap(mapId) - ENTRY POINT for loading a map (VdfLoad.cpp:395)
Resets state, resolves mapId -> m_mapDef via the map-def registry, opens the
portal-context load, stamps metric[0], then enters STATE_LOAD_CONTENT.
Logs "MapLoader: BeginMap - %u".

functions.name: VdfLoad_BeginTeleport
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::BeginTeleport - in-map relocation entry point (VdfLoad.cpp:358)
Unlike BeginMap this skips download/stream and jumps straight to
STATE_MODELS_STREAM (9). Requires MapPortalContextGet()->IsReady().
Stores destination m_spawnPos/m_spawnFacing and resolves m_portalIndex.

functions.name: VdfLoad_OnMapServerReady
functions.type: __int64 __fastcall(VdfLoad *this, __int64 serverAddrSrc, __int64 mapDef, __int64 a4, float *spawnPos, int spawnFacing, void *mapEncryptionKey, void *completionSink);
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::OnMapServerReady - map-server handoff callback (VdfLoad.cpp:426)
Asserts m_state is one of LOAD_CONTENT/LOAD_MANIFEST/SERVER_WAIT and that the
mapDef matches. Copies the server address into m_mapServerAddr (wchar_t[260]),
stores spawn point, encryption key and completion sink, then sets
m_serverReady = 1 which releases STATE_SERVER_WAIT -> STATE_MAP_DOWNLOAD.

functions.name: VdfLoad_ArePreloadAssetsReady
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::ArePreloadAssetsReady(&this->m_preloadModels)
Walks the two preload arrays (models at +0x268, textures at +0x288) and returns
nonzero only when every entry has finished loading. Polled by STATE_AGENT_STREAM.

functions.name: VdfLoad_Reset
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::Reset
Zeroes VdfLoadMetrics (0x38 bytes + mask), clears all state/timers, releases the
map-download object and every pending stream request.
Retail hang budgets (dev builds use 5000 for all three):
  m_modelsStreamBudgetMs = 60000
  m_assetStreamBudgetMs  = 15000
  m_agentStreamBudgetMs  = 120000

functions.name: VdfLoadMetrics_RecordTimestamp
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoadMetrics::RecordTimestamp(metric)
Stamps timeGetTime() into m_metrics[metric], but only the FIRST time that metric
is seen - m_setMask guards it. This is why the same call appears at the top of
every state handler yet each stage start is recorded once.
Most call sites are inlined; see the VdfLoadMetric enum for indices.

functions.name: VdfLoad_AssertValidViewState
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::AssertValidViewState (VdfLoad.cpp:1162-1177)
Debug precondition run at the top of every state handler: the active view must
not be any of the loading/cinematic views, and if WorldView()->HasRenderer()
then m_state must still be STATE_INIT. No-op in retail apart from the asserts.

functions.name: VdfLoadMetrics_RecordValue
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoadMetrics::RecordValue(metric, value)
Same first-write-wins semantics as RecordTimestamp but stores an arbitrary
value instead of a timestamp. Used for metric 12 (total models) and 13 (char count).

functions.name: VdfLoad_PreloadCharacterAssets
functions.rcmt:
VdfLoad::PreloadCharacterAssets
Called at the end of STATE_MAP_ASSET_STREAM. Looks up the local player's
race/profession row and force-loads its model + texture dependencies into
m_preloadModels / m_preloadTextures so the character is not popping in on the
first frame. VdfLoad__ArePreloadAssetsReady polls these during AGENT_STREAM.

functions.name: GrOcclusion_RegisterDynamicHandle
functions.rcmt:
CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::RegisterHandle  [Arena/Engine/Gr/GrLuid.cpp]

Allocates an occlusion handle for a DYNAMIC object and inserts its bounds into
the 2D LUID grid at (this+440).

Args: (mgr, userPtr, callbackOrOwner, aabbMin*, aabbMax*)

Slot allocation: pops a free slot off the freelist stack {ptr@+408, count@+420};
if empty, appends a new slot (m_handleCount @+196, cap @+220).  Warns once past
60000 dynamic objects ("Occlusion dynamic object count exceeded max of %i").

Parallel arrays grown to instanceCount (@+232):
  +240..+260  16-byte entries {u32 slot; u64 user}   <- m_occlusionInstances
  +272..+292  8-byte  user/owner pointers
  +304..+324  24-byte per-instance record (bounds)
  +336..+356  1-byte  per-instance flags/state

HANDLE ENCODING (see also UpdateHandleBounds / BindUserToStaticHandle):
  bit  31     1 = static (Umbra Tome) handle, 0 = dynamic
  bits 27..30 handleType (static handles only)
  bits 21..26 luid/tome generation id (& 0x3F)
  bits  0..20 handle array index (0x1FFFFF mask)
Returns the packed handle.

functions.name: GrLuid_GridInsertHandle
functions.rcmt:
LuidGrid::Insert  [Arena/Engine/Gr/GrLuid.cpp ~line 768]

Inserts an occlusion handle into every 2D grid cell its AABB overlaps.

1. FindHandleEntry(handle) -> existing entry; if it has flag 0x4000000 the object
   goes into m_specialCell (@+64) instead of the grid (huge/unbounded occluders).
2. Otherwise ProjectBoundsToCellRange() gives [minX,minY]..[maxX,maxY] cell span.
3. For each cell: index = x + m_gridDimensions.x * y  (asserts x < m_gridDimensions.x @+96,
   y < m_gridDimensions.y @+100), lazily AllocCell() into the cell pointer array @+8
   (count @+20), then appends the cell to the s_GrLuid_CellScratch list.
4. Each touched cell gets its sorted handle list binary-searched and re-sorted.
5. HashTableInsert(@+72) records handle -> touched-cell-set so removal is O(cells).

functions.type: void __fastcall(__int64 mgr, unsigned int staticHandle, __int64 userPtr, __int64 scenePtr);
functions.rcmt:
CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::BindUserToStaticHandle  [GrLuid.cpp ~1472]

Only acts on STATIC handles (a2 < 0, i.e. bit31 set):
  handleArrayIndex = handle & 0x1FFFFF
  handleType       = (handle >> 27) & 0xF     -> selects one of 16 32-byte buckets at a1
Grows m_occlusionInstances[handleType] (ptr @bucket+24, count @bucket+36) and stores
{user=a3, scene=a4} in the 16-byte slot.  Bumps the per-type live count at a1+176+4*type.

functions.name: GrOcclusion_UpdateHandleBounds
functions.rcmt:
CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::UpdateHandleBounds  [GrLuid.cpp]

Main-thread only.  Validates the handle against the current generation:
  (handle >> 21) & 0x3F == m_luidGeneration (@+432)
  handle is dynamic (bit31 clear)
  (handle & 0x1FFFFF) < m_handleCount (@+220/55*4)
then recomputes the object's AABB (negating Z to match Umbra's axis convention)
and re-inserts it into the LUID grid.  Silently ignores stale handles.

functions.name: GrDev_ResolveUmbraVisibility
functions.rcmt:
Arena\Engine\Gr\Dev\GrDevWin360.cpp  GrDevResolveUmbraVisibility()
(drawCtx, sortGroup, umbraTome, renderFlags)

The per-frame OCCLUSION CULL.  With no Tome loaded it falls straight through to
sub_140B08950(sortGroup) - the un-culled draw path.

With a Tome:
  1. Reads the current Gr camera; copies its position and NEGATES Z
     (cameraPosZNegated) - Umbra uses the opposite Z convention from Arena.
  2. Copies the view-projection matrix and builds an Umbra CameraTransform
     (Umbra_CameraTransform_Init).
  3. Sizes the shared visible-index array (s_UmbraVisibleArray_*) to
     Umbra_Tome_GetObjectCount(tome) + 1 and wraps it in an Umbra Visibility.
  4. Umbra_Query_ResolveVisibility(...,-1.0f); on failure retries with
     Umbra_Query_ResolveVisibilityFallback.  A non-zero error logs
     "Umbra query failed: %u" and falls back to the un-culled path.
  5. Walks the returned visible-index list and emits only those draw items.

Related: GrDev_IssueUmbraOcclusionQueries handles the GPU occlusion-query path
("umbra occlusion queries not supported on DX11"), and GrOcclusion_* /
GrLuid_Grid* own the object<->handle registry the Tome indices resolve against.

functions.name: ImgAtex_Decode
functions.cmt:
Arena\Engine\Gr\Img\ImgAtex.cpp  ImgAtex_Decode - ATEX-family texture decoder.

HOW TO READ THIS FUNCTION
It is a RESUMABLE STATE MACHINE, not a straight-line decoder. The caller feeds it
bytes as they arrive off disk; each entry runs `switch (state)` (cases 0..13), consumes
what it can, saves progress back into `decoder`, and returns. `savedState`, `savedMipLevel`
and `savedBlockIndex` are the resume point. Partial words that straddle a chunk boundary
are parked in spillWord / spillBits / spillByteCount.

Flow:
  1. read 4-byte container magic  -> containerMagic (ATEX ATTX ATEC ATEP ATEU ATET)
  2. read 4-byte pixel fourCC     -> formatFourCC   -> grFormat (GR_FORMAT enum)
  3. read width and height        -> imageWidth / imageHeight
  4. for each mip level: read the per-mip flags, then run the fill passes

decoder-> FIELD MAP (offsets from the decoder pointer)
  +0x00  input pointer               +0x28  per-level output pointer array
  +0x08  input bytes available       +0x30  bytes consumed so far
  +0x0C  total file size             +0x38  image width
  +0x10  target platform             +0x3C  image height
  +0x44  grFormat (GR_FORMAT enum)   +0x58  detail (private decoder state)
  +0x4C  containerTag  <-- WRITE-ONLY, see note below
  +0x60  fileType (0=ATEX 1=DDS 2=other)
  +0x70..+0x7C  spill state for partial words across chunk boundaries
  +0x80  block width     +0x88  level byte size   +0x8C  blocks across
  +0x90  bits per pixel  +0x94  current mip level

fourCC -> GR_FORMAT (read straight off the switch in this function)
  DXT1=22 DXT2=23 DXT3=24 DXT4=25 DXT5=26 DXTA=27 DXTL=28 DXTN=29
  3DCX=30 BC5X=31 BC7X=32 ; uncompressed 11CU..39CU = 2..21 ; GR_FORMATS = 38

THE CONTAINER TAG IS WRITE-ONLY
containerTag (ATEC=1 ATEP=2 ATEU=4 ATET=0x20) is computed here and stored at +0x4C,
and that is the ONLY place it is ever touched. Nothing reads it back - not this
function, not the loaders, not the image allocator. So ATEP decodes byte-for-byte
identically to ATEX. There is no premultiplied-alpha step and no other
container-driven pixel transform. If a .atep looks wrong, suspect the VIEWER
ignoring alpha, not this decoder.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES THE PIXELS
Only two things: the pixel fourCC above, and the per-mip flags dword -
  0x1 / 0x2 / 0x4 / 0x8  gate the RLE constant-fill passes
  0x10                   256x256 terrain border mirror (ImgAtex_MirrorTerrainBorders)
  0x200                  no block bitmap, mip is stored raw

NOTE ON VARIABLE NAMES: the header-parse and per-mip state variables are named.
The ~245 short-lived register temporaries inside the fill passes are left as vNN -
they are single-use arithmetic scratch, and naming them would be guesswork.

functions.cmt:
Arena\Engine\Gr\Bgfx\BgfxBuffer.cpp:406  GrFvf bitmask -> bgfx::VertexLayout.
THE definitive element order: the sequence of Add calls below IS the byte order in the
vertex. (attrib, num, type, normalized)  type: 0=Uint8 2=Int16 3=Half 4=Float
  0x00000001 POSITION        (0 Position,  3, Float)
  0x08000000 POSITION4       (0 Position,  4, Float)
  0x00000002 WEIGHTS         (9 Weight,    4, Uint8, normalized)
  0x00000004 GROUP           (8 Indices,   4, Uint8, RAW - bone indices)
  0x00000008 NORMAL          (1 Normal,    3, Float)
  0x04000000 NORMAL_C        (1 Normal,    4, Uint8, normalized)
  0x10000000 POSITION_COMPRESSED -> also emitted as (1 Normal, 4, Uint8, normalized)
  0x00000010 COLOR           (4 Color0,    4, Uint8, normalized)  BGRA order
  0x00000020 TANGENT         (2 Tangent,   3, Float)
  0x00000040 BITANGENT       (3 Bitangent, 3, Float)
  0x00000080 TANGENT_FRAME   -> THREE adds: Normal/Tangent/Bitangent, each 4 x Uint8 norm
  0x0000FF00 texcoords F32   (s_kTexCoordRemap[i], 2, Float)
  0x00FF0000 texcoords F16   (s_kTexCoordRemap[i], 2, Half)
TANGENT_FRAME is mutually exclusive with NORMAL|TANGENT|BITANGENT (asserted at :406).

functions.cmt:
Arena\Engine\Gr\Img\Atex\ImgAtexCommon.cpp:103  THE ATEX RLE CONSTANT-FILL DECODER.
  (cursor, detail)
This is the decode-side counterpart of the ImgAtex_EncodePlane_* passes, and the pass the
per-mip flag bits 0x1/0x2/0x4/0x8 switch on.

functions.cmt:
Arena\Engine\Map\MapData.cpp  register a map module. Asserts mapType < MAP_TYPES
and moduleInfo.id < s_maxModuleId.
functions.rcmt:
Arena\Engine\Map\MapData.cpp:1018  MapDataCreateNextModule()
(loadCtx, wantEditorFlags)

One step of the map-load state machine: creates the SINGLE module at the current
cursor (loadCtx+648) for loadCtx's mapType (+608, asserts < MAP_TYPES==4), then
advances the cursor.  Called repeatedly until the cursor passes the module count.

Per step:
  desc = g_MapModulesByType[mapType].ptr[cursor]        (56-byte descriptor)
  skip unless desc->mapTypeMask (+16) has this mapType's bit set (_bittest)
  createParams = { 0x45C00000, 0x45C00000, <bounds from loadCtx+628>, 32 }
  wantEditorFlags != 0  ->  createParams.flags |= 0xFC1
  instance = desc->Create(loadCtx->mapObj@+552, createParams, loadCtx->loader@+544)

Success: mapObj->vtbl[320](mapObj, desc->id, instance) registers the instance;
         asserts desc->id < s_maxModuleId.
Failure: unwinds every module already created (vtbl[304] fetch, desc->Shutdown@+40),
         releases the map via vtbl[296], and sets loadCtx state (+624) = 5.
Cursor exhausted: sub_140C32010(loader) and state (+624) = 4.

Was previously named MapData_RegisterModule - it creates one module, it does not
register the module type; the type registry is MapData_AddModule.

functions.name: MapData_DestroyModulesReverse
functions.rcmt:
Arena\Engine\Map\MapData.cpp:548  MapDataDestroyModules()
(mapType, moduleCount, instances)

Teardown, NOT a getter (the old name MapData_GetModule was wrong).
Walks g_MapModulesByType[mapType] backwards (descIter -= 56 bytes per entry) and for
each module with a live instance calls desc->Shutdown (desc+40), then nulls
instances[moduleId].  Asserts ptr->id < moduleCount.
Reverse order guarantees dependents are torn down before their dependencies.

Fails hard with "Dependency-sorting failed." -- a module cycle is fatal, not skipped.
functions.rcmt:
MapData::DependencySortModules  [Arena/Engine/Map/MapData.cpp]

One-time (guarded by g_MapModulesRegistered + g_MapModulesCritSec) registration of
every map-data module, then a topological sort per map type.  "Dependency-sorting
failed." is fatal - a cycle aborts, it is not skipped.

Each MapMod_<Name>_GetDesc() returns a static 56-byte descriptor:
  +0   u32   moduleId          (bit index used in the dependency masks)
  +8   char* name             ("Prop", "Terrain", "Zone", ...)
  +16  u32   mapTypeMask      1=client-only, 3=client+?, 7=all 4 MAP_TYPES
  +20  u32   dependencyMask   bitmask of moduleIds that must load first
  +24  u32   dependencyMask   (duplicate of +20)
  +28  u32   0 / 0x10000 / 0xFFFFFFFF
  +32  fn    Create(alloc, params, ...)      <- called by MapData_RegisterModule
  +40  fn    Shutdown()                       <- called by MapData_DestroyModulesReverse
  +48  fn    LoadChunk(module, packFile, map) <- pulls this module's chunk out of the .map

Registered modules and their .map pack-file chunk tags:
   0 Audio         'audi'   deps: Environment
   1 Block         'bloc'   deps: Params

  15 Occlusion     'octm'   deps: Params            <- Umbra Tome chunk
  16 Params        'parm'   deps: (none)            <- root module
  17 Prop          'prp2'   deps: Params

functions.name: PrDataImport_ImportPropData
functions.rcmt:
Arena\Engine\Map\Prop\PrDataImport.cpp:548  PrDataImportImportPropData()
(propCtx, pack, importFlags)

Turns the decoded 'prp2' chunk (g_PackDef_PackMapProp) into live PrProp objects -
this is where every statically-placed 3D model in a map comes from.
materialCtx comes from map->vtbl[384] once and is threaded into every fill.

Three passes over the pack, one per array, each with the same tail:
  1. pack->propArray          count @+0,  ptr @+4,  stride 118  (PackMapPropObj)
  2. pack->propAnimArray      count @+12, ptr @+16, stride 126  (PackMapPropObjAnimSeq)
                              -- 118 + 8; the extra qword @+118 is animSequence,
                                 pushed via prop->vtbl[96], and also recorded in the
                                 anim-sequence map at propCtx+40/+48
  3. pack->propInstanceArray  count @+24, ptr @+28, stride 142  (PackMapPropObjInstance)
                              -- asserts !isOverride; allocates the prop itself
                                 (0x190 bytes, memcat 9, tag 400), then walks
                                 origGuidArray (count @+130, ptr @+134) into the
                                 original-GUID map at propCtx+136/+144

Common tail per record:
  prop = PrDataImport_CreatePropFromPack(propCtx, packProp+32, importFlags)
  PrDataImport_FillPropFromPack(prop, packProp, materialCtx)
  bucketId = *(u16*)(packProp + 112)   -- PackMapPropObj.bucketId
  propCtx->bucketArray[bucketId] = prop            (array @+312/320, count @+332)
  guidHash = Hash(prop->guid)                      -- prop+8 is the GUID
  insert into the prop GUID hash (@+64, slots @+112, count @+124, mask @+128);
  after 5 probe collisions it calls PrDataImport_GrowPropHashTable.
  propCtx->propCount (@+32) is incremented for every prop created.

Per-prop culling/LOD behaviour comes from PackMapPropObj.flags (see the
MapPropFlags enum / g_MapPropFlagNames) plus lod1/lod2 fade distances, which
PrContext_LoadPropModel later turns into the lodDistances[4] array it hands to
ModelMgr_LoadModel.  broadId (@PackMapPropObj) is the prop's slot in the
MapPropBroadphase built by PrDataImport_CreateBroadphase.

functions.name: ZnContext_UpdateCameraAndCull
functions.rcmt:
ZnContext::UpdateCamera  [Arena/Engine/Map/Zones/ZnContext.cpp]

Per-frame driver for the whole zone (scattered-model) system.  a2 is a camera block:
  +0  float3 cameraPos
  +12 float3 axisX      (or frustum corner ray)
  +24 float3 axisY
  +36 float3 axisZ
  +48 int    flags      -> cached at this+1716; bit1 gates chunk population

   1536-unit zone chunks now inside the cull rect.
4. profile "MapZoneUpdateCamera" -> ZnChunk_UpdateCamera(this+200, ...)  -- LOD /
   fade / per-instance distance work for the chunks that survived.
5. ZnChunk_PushModelToFreeingList drain (this+1432), then map->vtbl[168].

filling the visible-zone index array at this+1800/count this+1812, and resets the
active-zone bookkeeping at this+1780.

happens to work when Cmp_DistExtraBits[0]==0 but desyncs whenever

functions.name: Cpt_ExpandKeyTo20
functions.cmt:
Key expansion: an 8-byte strs password -> the 20-byte key actually fed to RC4.
  (keyBytes, keyPtr, dstArray)
1. fill 20 bytes cyclically: dst[i] = key[i % keyBytes]
2. XOR in any key bytes past 20 (never happens for the 8-byte strs keys)
3. ONE SHA-1-shaped round over the 5 dwords, ROL5 / ROL30, constants
   -1615554381, 1722862861, 0x22222222, 0x7BF36AE2, -214083945,
   0x59D148C0, -696916869, -1269579175
Not a standard SHA-1 - it is one custom round, so it must be ported literally.

functions.name: Archive_MakeFileNameFromFileId
functions.rcmt:
FileArchive.cpp:720  MakeFileName(fileId, wchar_t out[4], uint8 subFile)
Encodes a fileId as a 2-3 code-unit UTF-16 'filename' (base-0xFF00 digits, each biased +0x100):
  out[1] = (fileId-1) / 0xFF00 + 0x100   // high digit
  out[0] = (fileId-1) % 0xFF00 + 0x100   // low digit
  out[2] = subFile ? subFile + 0x100 : 0 ; out[3] = 0
Bias keeps every code unit >= 0x100 so an id-name can never collide with a real path.
EXACT INVERSE of Archive_ExtractFileIdFromFileName (0x140DB6CD0).

functions.name: Archive_ExtractFileIdFromFileName
functions.rcmt:
FileArchive.cpp:702  ExtractArchiveFileId(const wchar_t* name, uint8* outSubFile)
Decodes the base-0xFF00 filename back to the fileId - fully reversible, no information lost:
  fileId = 0xFF00 * name[1] + name[0] - 0xFF00FF
  subFile = name[2] ? (uint8)name[2] : 0
Returns 0 if the string is not an id-name (name[0] < 0x100 || name[1] < 0x100 ||
(name[2] != 0 && (name[2] < 0x100 || name[3] != 0))).
Valid range: fileId 1 .. 0xFE010000 (4261478400). Inverse of 0x140DB6C40.

functions.cmt:
Arena\Services\Token\Token.cpp:30  32-bit token -> lowercase name. THIS IS NOT A HASH.
  v = (token - 0x30000000) mod 2^32
  while (v) { *out++ = Token_Base23Alphabet[v % 23]; v /= 23; }
Base 23, alphabet "abcdefghiklmnopvrstuwxy" (no j/q/z; note the order ...o,p,v,r,s,t,u).
It is fully REVERSIBLE - encode by running the base-23 digits back and adding 0x30000000.
Because 23^7 just exceeds 2^32, every name is at most 7 characters.
Used for MODL material constant names and engine-global shader params (grblcol, ...).

functions.name: TextDecode_DecodeRecord
functions.cmt:
TextDecode.cpp  the core record decoder - decrypt then bit-unpack.
  (decoder, textContext, stringId, record, key8)
Record header is u16[]: [0] = total length (>= 6), [1] = baseChar, byte[4] = rangeBits,
payload = record+3, payload length = record[0] - 6.

IF key8 != 0:  Cpt_ExpandKeyTo20(8, &key8) -> CptRc4_Create -> CptRc4_Crypt over the payload
ELSE:          the payload is copied verbatim

Then, if baseChar == 0 && rangeBits == 16 && the length is even, the payload IS raw UTF-16
and is passed straight through. Otherwise bit-unpack, LSB first, refilling while the
accumulator holds <= 0x18 bits:
    sym = acc & ((1 << rangeBits) - 1)
    sym == 0        -> NUL terminator
    sym in 1..31    -> TextDecode_SymbolTable[sym - 1]
    sym >= 0x20     -> (wchar)(sym + baseChar - 32)

functions.name: TextDecode_DecodeString
functions.cmt:
Gw2\Engine\Text\TextDecode.cpp:217  decode one string by id. THE ENTRY POINT.
  (decoder, stringId, record) -> wide string
1. validate the source buffer (TextParser_Validate)
2. TextParser_FindEmbeddedKey - a parent string may carry the key in a control code
3. otherwise look the key up in the runtime key map at textContext+512
     slot = Arena_OpenAddrFindSlot(map, &stringId); 24-byte entries
     { u32 id@0, u64 key8@8, u32 occupied@16 }
4. TextDecode_DecodeRecord with whatever key was found (0 = plaintext record)
The key map is populated at RUNTIME (server messages / TextPack chunks), which is why a
strs file pulled straight out of Gw2.dat cannot be decrypted offline without captured keys.

functions.cmt:
Gw2\Game\Scene\Cli\ScnCliContext.cpp:222,317  THE SUBTITLE PATH.
A "chatter line" is a spoken line with an on-screen caption. Takes a
codedSpeakerName + codedText pair (both still text-coded; TextDecode_* resolves
them) and a chatterLineType asserted <= Content::CHATTER_LINE_TYPES (201).
Duration comes from ScnCli_GetChatterLineDuration, picking a near or far value
depending on whether the speaker is the player's current target.
Type 7 is special-cased: 30 s suppression window instead of 60 s, and a 500 ms
re-show delay instead of 5000 ms.
If the speaker agent exists the line goes to its overhead bubble; otherwise it is
drawn as a standalone caption. "Cinecaption" (0x1422E52A0) is the font style used.

functions.rcmt:
MmRenderManager::DrawMarkerLayers - draws 2D map / compass ICONS.
Iterates marker->GetMarkerDef() across [layerFirst, layerTerm) so markers paint
in layer order - this layer ordering is what produces the map legend grouping.
MmRenderManager__SetEdgeRectangle / __SetEdgeCircle choose how off-screen
markers are clamped to the compass edge (RENDER_EDGE_TYPE_RECTANGLE/CIRCLE).

Logs "Unable to find floor %i". m_dataFloor is the current floor record;
WorldMapManager__UpdateFloorState runs the m_floorState machine that swaps
floors, and WorldMapInterior__LoadInteriorOverlay pulls interior overlay art
by interior->filename.

functions.name: WmItemImagePaged_BuildLayerImage
functions.rcmt:
WmItemImagePaged::BuildLayerImage - 2D world map tile layer builder.
Fails with "Unknown layer image type" on an unrecognised layer.
The 2D map is a paged texture grid: WmItemImagePaged__InitChunkGrid asserts
referenceSize % CHUNK_TEXTURE_RESOLUTION == 0, WmItemImagePaged__UpdateChunkStates
drives each chunk's load state machine, and WorldMapCoverage__GetZoomCoverage
indexes m_coverage[zoom] to decide which chunks a zoom level needs.

WmMapLabel::OnCreateMsg - 2D map text LABEL widget factory.
Asserts createParams.object->GetWorldMapModel()->GetModelType() ==
WORLD_MAP_MODEL_TYPE_LABEL. WmPointOfInterest__OnCreateMsg is the sibling for
POI icons (waypoints, vistas, hearts).

VdfLoad::Update - MAP LOADING STATE MACHINE (VdfLoad.cpp:347)
Driven once per frame with deltaMs. Dispatches on this->m_state (VdfLoadState).

Flow:
  0  INIT
  1  LOAD_CONTENT      inline here - waits on map content pack, pushes m_mapDef to portal ctx
  2  LOAD_MANIFEST     inline here - waits MapPortalContext::IsReady(), arms 300s server wait
  3  SERVER_WAIT       inline here - waits m_serverReady (set by VdfLoad__OnMapServerReady)
  4  SERVER_WAIT_ERROR terminal (timeout)
  5  MAP_DOWNLOAD      -> VdfLoad__State05_MapDownload
  6  DOWNLOAD_ERROR    terminal
  7  MAP_STREAM        -> VdfLoad__State07_MapStream
  8  MAP_STREAM_ERROR  terminal
  9  MODELS_STREAM     -> VdfLoad__State09_ModelsStream
  10 MAP_ASSET_STREAM  inline here - min() of per-map completion until 1.0, then preloads char assets
  11 AGENT_STREAM      -> VdfLoad__State11_AgentStream
  12 READY_WAIT        -> VdfLoad__State12_ReadyWait
  13 READY             terminal - map is playable

Hang detection: each state arms the NEXT state's budge

VdfLoad state 11: STATE_AGENT_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:926)
Arms m_readyWaitTimerMs = 1000 and ticks m_agentStreamTimerMs.
Waits for the agent-view to report ready, then for character loading to drain
(char count == 0) and VdfLoad__ArePreloadAssetsReady. Records metric 12
(total models) and 13 (char count). Pushes the terrain/env params into every
m_maps entry, then -> STATE_READY_WAIT.

VdfLoad state 5: STATE_MAP_DOWNLOAD (VdfLoad.cpp:556)
Ticks m_mapDownloadTimerMs. Polls m_mapDownload; on failure -> state 6.
Rejects encrypted maps (mapDef flags & 0x20000000) when m_mapEncryptionKey is
NULL: "tried to enter an encrypted map without a key".
On success builds m_streamRequests (56-byte entries) and spawns one map-stream
object per request into m_maps, then -> STATE_MAP_STREAM.

VdfLoad state 7: STATE_MAP_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:691)
Arms m_modelsStreamBudgetMs -> m_modelsStreamTimerMs for the next state.
Polls each m_streamRequests[i] status (vtbl+48): 1/2/3 stamp metrics 5/6/7 and
re-issue with priority 100; 4 = done -> publishes the built map into m_maps[i];
5 = error -> state 8. Releases each request once consumed.
When all are done: VdfLoad__ActivateMapsAndBuildWorld, then STATE_MODELS_STREAM.

VdfLoad state 9: STATE_MODELS_STREAM (VdfLoad.cpp:766)
Arms m_assetStreamBudgetMs and ticks m_modelsStreamTimerMs.
For the first 6000ms (0x1770) it keeps re-sampling the global model counters to
establish m_modelLoadTotal; after that the total is frozen so the progress bar
cannot go backwards. m_modelCompletion is monotonic (never decreases).
Teleports (m_portalIndex != -1) take completion straight from the portal ctx.
Exits when completion >= 1.0 OR the timer expires (logs a hang), -> ASSET_STREAM.

VdfLoad state 12: STATE_READY_WAIT (VdfLoad.cpp:1003)
One-second settle: while m_readyWaitTimerMs > 0 it keeps pushing lighting/env
parameters into each map so the first presented frame is fully lit.
When it expires: closes the portal context, notifies the world view, marks each
map active (vtbl+168, arg 2) and -> STATE_READY. Map is now playable.

VdfLoad::ActivateMapsAndBuildWorld (VdfLoad.cpp:1095)
Called once at the end of STATE_MAP_STREAM. Binds each streamed map to the
local player's agent, registers the map id with the audio/env systems, creates
the world renderer and seeds the camera from m_spawnPos.
Asserts !WorldView()->HasRenderer() on entry - the renderer must not exist yet.

VdfLoad::BeginMap(mapId) - ENTRY POINT for loading a map (VdfLoad.cpp:395)
Resets state, resolves mapId -> m_mapDef via the map-def registry, opens the
portal-context load, stamps metric[0], then enters STATE_LOAD_CONTENT.
Logs "MapLoader: BeginMap - %u".

VdfLoad::BeginTeleport - in-map relocation entry point (VdfLoad.cpp:358)
Unlike BeginMap this skips download/stream and jumps straight to
STATE_MODELS_STREAM (9). Requires MapPortalContextGet()->IsReady().
Stores destination m_spawnPos/m_spawnFacing and resolves m_portalIndex.

VdfLoad::OnMapServerReady - map-server handoff callback (VdfLoad.cpp:426)
Asserts m_state is one of LOAD_CONTENT/LOAD_MANIFEST/SERVER_WAIT and that the
mapDef matches. Copies the server address into m_mapServerAddr (wchar_t[260]),
stores spawn point, encryption key and completion sink, then sets
m_serverReady = 1 which releases STATE_SERVER_WAIT -> STATE_MAP_DOWNLOAD.

VdfLoad::ArePreloadAssetsReady(&this->m_preloadModels)
Walks the two preload arrays (models at +0x268, textures at +0x288) and returns
nonzero only when every entry has finished loading. Polled by STATE_AGENT_STREAM.

VdfLoad::Reset
Zeroes VdfLoadMetrics (0x38 bytes + mask), clears all state/timers, releases the
map-download object and every pending stream request.
Retail hang budgets (dev builds use 5000 for all three):
  m_modelsStreamBudgetMs = 60000
  m_assetStreamBudgetMs  = 15000
  m_agentStreamBudgetMs  = 120000

VdfLoadMetrics::RecordTimestamp(metric)
Stamps timeGetTime() into m_metrics[metric], but only the FIRST time that metric
is seen - m_setMask guards it. This is why the same call appears at the top of
every state handler yet each stage start is recorded once.
Most call sites are inlined; see the VdfLoadMetric enum for indices.

VdfLoad::AssertValidViewState (VdfLoad.cpp:1162-1177)
Debug precondition run at the top of every state handler: the active view must
not be any of the loading/cinematic views, and if WorldView()->HasRenderer()
then m_state must still be STATE_INIT. No-op in retail apart from the asserts.

VdfLoadMetrics::RecordValue(metric, value)
Same first-write-wins semantics as RecordTimestamp but stores an arbitrary
value instead of a timestamp. Used for metric 12 (total models) and 13 (char count).

VdfLoad::PreloadCharacterAssets
Called at the end of STATE_MAP_ASSET_STREAM. Looks up the local player's
race/profession row and force-loads its model + texture dependencies into
m_preloadModels / m_preloadTextures so the character is not popping in on the
first frame. VdfLoad__ArePreloadAssetsReady polls these during AGENT_STREAM.

HANDLE ENCODING (see also UpdateHandleBounds / BindUserToStaticHandle):

GrOcclusion: load/validate the Umbra Tome PropIDMap  [GrLuid.cpp]

Maps exported prop IDs to Tome occlusion object IDs.  Two failure paths both
disable precomputed occlusion and fall back to Umbra OB (Occlusion Booster,
the runtime occlusion path):
  "PropIDMap element count did not match calculated count.  Disabling Tome."
  "Version mis-match with a PropIDMap.  Re-export the data to update.  Falling back to Umbra OB"

LuidGrid::Insert  [Arena/Engine/Gr/GrLuid.cpp ~line 768]

Inserts an occlusion handle into every 2D grid cell its AABB overlaps.

1. FindHandleEntry(handle) -> existing entry; if it has flag 0x4000000 the object
   goes into m_specialCell (@+64) instead of the grid (huge/unbounded occluders).
2. Otherwise ProjectBoundsToCellRange() gives [minX,minY]..[maxX,maxY] cell span.
3. For each cell: index = x + m_gridDimensions.x * y  (asserts x < m_gridDimensions.x @+96,
   y < m_gridDimensions.y @+100), lazily AllocCell() into the cell pointer array @+8
   (count @+20), then appends the cell to the s_GrLuid_CellScratch list.
4. Each touched cell gets its sorted handle list binary-searched and re-sorted.
5. HashTableInsert(@+72) records handle -> touched-cell-set so removal is O(cells).

CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::BindUserToStaticHandle  [GrLuid.cpp ~1472]

Only acts on STATIC handles (a2 < 0, i.e. bit31 set):
  handleArrayIndex = handle & 0x1FFFFF
  handleType       = (handle >> 27) & 0xF     -> selects one of 16 32-byte buckets at a1
Grows m_occlusionInstances[handleType] (ptr @bucket+24, count @bucket+36) and stores
{user=a3, scene=a4} in the 16-byte slot.  Bumps the per-type live count at a1+176+4*type.

CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::BindUserToAllStaticWater  [GrLuid.cpp ~1780]

Requires TomeHasStaticWater() (m_tomeStaticWaterCount @+436).  Walks every static
water occlusion instance in handleType bucket 0 (array @+80, count @+100) and binds
(user, scene) into each 16-byte {user,scene} slot.  Asserts a slot is not already
bound.  Returns a synthetic STATIC handle:  (generation | 0xFFFFFC80) << 21
(bit31 set marks it static/tome-owned).

CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::UnRegisterHandle  [GrLuid.cpp]

Main-thread only.  Range-checks the handle (logs "...incoming handle was outside of
the range of allocated handles."), removes it from every LUID grid cell, clears the
instance slot, and pushes the slot index back onto the freelist stack @+408/+420.

CIGrOcclusionObjectManager::UpdateHandleBounds  [GrLuid.cpp]

Main-thread only.  Validates the handle against the current generation:
  (handle >> 21) & 0x3F == m_luidGeneration (@+432)
  handle is dynamic (bit31 clear)
  (handle & 0x1FFFFF) < m_handleCount (@+220/55*4)
then recomputes the object's AABB (negating Z to match Umbra's axis convention)
and re-inserts it into the LUID grid.  Silently ignores stale handles.

containerTag (ATEC=1 ATEP=2 ATEU=4 ATET=0x20) -> decoder+0x4C.

an .atep decodes byte-for-byte the same as an .atex.

One step of the map-load state machine: creates the SINGLE module at the current
cursor (loadCtx+648) for loadCtx's mapType (+608, asserts < MAP_TYPES==4), then
advances the cursor.  Called repeatedly until the cursor passes the module count.

Per step:
  desc = g_MapModulesByType[mapType].ptr[cursor]        (56-byte descriptor)
  skip unless desc->mapTypeMask (+16) has this mapType's bit set (_bittest)
  createParams = { 0x45C00000, 0x45C00000, <bounds from loadCtx+628>, 32 }
  wantEditorFlags != 0  ->  createParams.flags |= 0xFC1
  instance = desc->Create(loadCtx->mapObj@+552, createParams, loadCtx->loader@+544)

Success: mapObj->vtbl[320](mapObj, desc->id, instance) registers the instance;
         asserts desc->id < s_maxModuleId.
Failure: unwinds every module already created (vtbl[304] fetch, desc->Shutdown@+40),

(mapType, moduleCount, instances)

Teardown, NOT a getter (the old name MapData_GetModule was wrong).

each module with a live instance calls desc->Shutdown (desc+40), then nulls

Per-frame driver for the whole zone (scattered-model) system.  a2 is a camera block:

ZnContext::CullZones ("MapZoneCull")

DISTANCE culling, not frustum culling: builds an axis-aligned square in map XY
centred on the camera with half-extent = fminf(m_zoneDrawDistance @this+1824, a3),
snaps it to the 1536-unit chunk grid (ZnChunk_SnapRectToChunkGrid), and early-outs
if the snapped rect is unchanged from last frame (cached at this+1700..1712).

On change it re-queries the zone broadphase (this+1856, vtbl[24]) with the rect,
filling the visible-zone index array at this+1800/count this+1812, and resets the
active-zone bookkeeping at this+1780.

ZnChunk::PopulateChunks  [Arena/Engine/Map/Zones/ZnChunk.cpp]

Streams zone chunks in and out for the cull rect computed by
ZnContext_CullZonesByCameraRect.  For each newly-entered chunk it runs the
procedural placement (ZnPlacement_ScatterInstances / ZnPlacement_TileScatterFill),
subtracting the blocker polygons registered through ZnChunk_AddBlockerPolygon
(m_blockerPolygonsBroadphase) so scattered ground cover does not grow through

onto the freeing list (ZnChunk_PushModelToFreeingList) for deferred release.

THE MAIN DECISION OF THE WHOLE DECOMPRESSOR.
symbol < 0x100  -> it is a plain byte, write it straight to the output.
symbol >= 0x100 -> it is a 'go back and repeat' instruction; the next steps read
                   how MANY bytes to repeat (length) and how FAR BACK to start
                   (distance), then copy that run forward.

FileArchive.cpp:720  MakeFileName(fileId, wchar_t out[4], uint8 subFile)
Encodes a fileId as a 2-3 code-unit UTF-16 'filename' (base-0xFF00 digits, each biased +0x100):
  out[1] = (fileId-1) / 0xFF00 + 0x100   // high digit
  out[0] = (fileId-1) % 0xFF00 + 0x100   // low digit
  out[2] = subFile ? subFile + 0x100 : 0 ; out[3] = 0
Bias keeps every code unit >= 0x100 so an id-name can never collide with a real path.
EXACT INVERSE of Archive_ExtractFileIdFromFileName (0x140DB6CD0).

FileArchive.cpp:702  ExtractArchiveFileId(const wchar_t* name, uint8* outSubFile)
Decodes the base-0xFF00 filename back to the fileId - fully reversible, no information lost:
  fileId = 0xFF00 * name[1] + name[0] - 0xFF00FF
  subFile = name[2] ? (uint8)name[2] : 0
Returns 0 if the string is not an id-name (name[0] < 0x100 || name[1] < 0x100 ||
(name[2] != 0 && (name[2] < 0x100 || name[3] != 0))).
Valid range: fileId 1 .. 0xFE010000 (4261478400). Inverse of 0x140DB6C40.

MmRenderManager::DrawMarkerLayers - draws 2D map / compass ICONS.
Iterates marker->GetMarkerDef() across [layerFirst, layerTerm) so markers paint
in layer order - this layer ordering is what produces the map legend grouping.
MmRenderManager__SetEdgeRectangle / __SetEdgeCircle choose how off-screen
markers are clamped to the compass edge (RENDER_EDGE_TYPE_RECTANGLE/CIRCLE).

WorldMapManager::FindFloor - resolves a map floor (multi-level maps).
Logs "Unable to find floor %i". m_dataFloor is the current floor record;
WorldMapManager__UpdateFloorState runs the m_floorState machine that swaps
floors, and WorldMapInterior__LoadInteriorOverlay pulls interior overlay art
by interior->filename.

WmItemImagePaged::BuildLayerImage - 2D world map tile layer builder.
Fails with "Unknown layer image type" on an unrecognised layer.
The 2D map is a paged texture grid: WmItemImagePaged__InitChunkGrid asserts
referenceSize % CHUNK_TEXTURE_RESOLUTION == 0, WmItemImagePaged__UpdateChunkStates
drives each chunk's load state machine, and WorldMapCoverage__GetZoomCoverage
indexes m_coverage[zoom] to decide which chunks a zoom level needs.

comments.cmt:
ImgFmt_Flags: dword[38] capability bits per GR_FORMAT.
  0x001  block compressed (4x4); drives ImgFmt_GetBlockDims
  0x210 / 0x280  select which PLANES a block carries. ImgAtex_Encode derives the block
         size from them:  planeDwords = (flags&0x280 ?2:0) + (flags&0x210 ?2:0)
                                      + (format==GR_FORMAT_DXTL ?2:0)
         and planeDwords*4 == bytes per block, cross-checked against bpp*16/8:
           DXT1 0x071 -> 0x210 only            ->  8 bytes  (1 colour block)
           DXTA 0x0a1 -> 0x280 only            ->  8 bytes  (1 alpha block)
           DXT2..5, BC7 0x0b1 -> both          -> 16 bytes  (alpha + colour)
           DXTN/3DC/BC5 0x201 -> both          -> 16 bytes  (two channels)
           DXTL 0x011 -> 0x210 + the DXTL case -> 16 bytes
This is why the ATEX container needs no per-format decoder: the flags tell it how many
8-byte planes a block has, and it moves blocks, never texels.

comments.cmt:
CmpHuff_BootSymTbl: 768 bytes = THREE 256-byte sections, all indexed by the same key
  index = (runLength << 5) | codeLength    (runLength 0..7, codeLength 0..31)
  [  0..255]  DECODE: one packed byte per entry, (runLength << 5) | codeLength
  [256..511]  ENCODE: how many bits the bootstrap code occupies
  [512..767]  ENCODE: the bootstrap code value itself
So it is a bidirectional codec table, not just the decode half. Decode side is read by
CmpHuff_BuildDecodeTable; encode side by CmpHuff_WriteRunLengthCode.
